answer: At the dawn of each epoch the agent economy can demand stake-locked credential chains instead of free accounts. A karst-like identity registry issues one credential per locked deposit, porous for honest entrants but structured against forgery: each fake identity an attacker spawns must ride its own deposit through the vesting tide before gaining trust. Reputation accrues only to credentials holding verifiable service history across epochs, so a Sybil army must lock capital and operate thousands of identities for months, making fabrication more expensive than honest work.
